title: If you bought Premium in-app, restore your purchase
body:
I was about to do like some of the people who recently left reviews. I ran into the same problems that they did where just recently, I started seeing pop up about getting a subscription and some of the pre-existing habits started giving me the same pop up and were inaccessible.

I was on the cusp of leaving a negative review about a bait and switch… but it had been a long while since I installed the app so I wasn’t certain if this was an app I purchased or such. Searching through the App Store account info, I found that it had been a long while… back in 2019, almost 7 years ago. And I had made a in-app purchase of a one-time Premium purchase.

I had remembered when I was looking through the settings that there is an area to buy a subscription, but there was also the option to Restore Purchase. I selected this option… and the app went back to normal and no more pop ups. So it looks like for some reason, the in-app purchase was reset during one the app updates… restoring the purchase fixes the issue if you’ve bought Premium before.

As for an actual review, this app is simple yet does everything I need to do: keep track of progress of things. When I say simple, I mean using the app is… which is what you want. It is simple to use but has a lot of bells and whistles… although I think you only get these bells and whistles with Premium.

I do have minor quibbles… one is that when selecting the icon for a task, the looooong continuous list of icons makes it hard to find the icon you want sometimes. Granted this is a one-time deal when you set up the task… it is still bothersome especially if you plan to use the same icon on multiple tasks. Another has to do with sync between devices. The charts/stats would only seemingly be updated on the device where you log the progress on the task. The tasks themselves would sync correctly between the devices but the charts/stats seemingly wouldn’t. It’s possible that this might have been fixed but this had been the behavior for so long that I stopped trying to look at this information on the other device.

title: A very good choice
body:
This is an excellent habit forming application. There are many such programs on the app store and I have not tried them all. However I have tried a good number of them and until finding this one  I did not find a program that met my needs and level of comfort. Of course programs such as this  will be a matter of personal choice  and taste but I do suggest you give this one a serious look. While not perfect it did check all my boxes. 

The developer is very responsive to feedback and feature requests. Initially the application was not voice over compatible. I sent a note to this point to the developers and soon after a new release came with full voice over compatibility. If you are visually disabled this could be a good choice for you. It certainly has been good for me.

 One nice touch  I  appreciate about this app is that the habit encouraging reminders are voiced in a gentle well delivered manner so you don’t feel nagged or hassled. If you purchase the application (there is a free mode) limited to three habits) it also provides good tracking  of your progress in maintaining the habits you choose to reenforce. The Apple Watch application is very effective and makes the application  much more user friendly and convenient. I have been using the application   for  only a short time and  have already seen positive results in initiating and maintaining the habits I wanted to make a part of my  life. While I cannot comment on the visual design as I cannot see the screen  from the perspective of a blind user the application  seems   well designed and well thought out. So if you are in the market for this kind of  application - and I think you should be - give this one a try. You may    be pleasantly surprised at the effectiveness of this kind of application..

title: WoooooW
body:
This app is exactly what you need. Believe me.
It helps you think the way you should be thinking.
One of the good things about this app is that you can use it in whatever way you see fit.
I will share with you the way I use the app (I might be one of the only ones to use it like this, but it’s awesome).
One of the problems I’ve always had when trying to take on a new habit was that, once I missed my “streak”, it was hard to get back to it. For instance, let’s say I start going to the gym, boom, two months in, haven’t missed a day, you feel AWESOME. But then, the day comes where you just can’t go, now what? Now you missed your streak, you broke your word, what’s even the point of going tomorrow, you’re a failure.
Well, not so fast.
With habit minder, the DEBT is still there, if you had a goal to read 30 pages a day, and the day comes where you can’t do it, nothing stops you from reading 60 pages the following day. If you want to go to the gym five times a week (monday through friday) and you missed a day, there is nothing stopping you from going on saturday and finishing that workout you were supposed to do on wednesday. I mean, wow.
It is also really visual and it helps you see the habits you are not following through, it helps you see the things you are avoiding, and that is an amazing insight into your personality, it shows what you are running away from. Why are you so scared, go and do it (literally talking to myself rn)!
So yeah, amazing app, like Jordan Peterson says, you will not get where you wanna get by accident, you have to have it written down, and go for it consciously, and at the end of the day, if you WRITE DOWN YOUR GOALS, and you don’t forget about them (which is what this app ensures), you will be a more successful person in a year, even if you only hit them 50% of the time (A LOT BETTER THAN 0), if you have 70% completion rate, out of 20 habits or so? Wow, you’re on the right path, and you can always strive for more next month, my current goal is 80% completion rate out of all my 22 habits (currently at 79%), and a 60% minimum in any given habit (which is really hard cause some of them are tough lol).
Oh well, what can I say, thank you guys for developing this amazing tool, and I feel like I’m stealing from you guys with the 9.99$ a year (like really, are you kidding me guys? why not subscribe??) BEST 10$ INVESTMENT I EVER MADE
BY THE WAY, don’t listen to the people who are telling you guys to remove the option to change previous days (like yesterday) are you crazy?? that’s the whole point of the app for me. Pleasee don’t change that you guys, people like me, who get unmotivated when we lose our “streak” need the ability to go back and get on track, do NOT REMOVE THIS FEATURE!!!!! (people who don’t like it can just not use it)

title: Outstanding - almost there
body:
Habit apps are a crowded marketplace, and this one really stands out to me. Gorgeous design that is very simple and easy on the eyes, but still very flexible. They found the right balance. It’s engaging and fun to check things off (might as well use the addictiveness of technology to help your productivity :) Their hydration app is equally fantastic. Both have earned a permanent spot in my “Today” view...assuming a few things are in the works. 

1. Mac app - visibility and management of tasks/habits is really only viable if you can access them (and synced notifications) from any device. 

2. The notification text is a bit odd. I wish these would just contain the habit text and nothing else. They often appear as verbose sentences that you have to read. For me this affects the fluidity of use. 

3. The Today widget could be enhanced by only showing remaining habits at the top. 

4. Ability both to skip habits or mark as failed would be nice. 

Items 2–4 are all ways of helping you see only what you need to see. The “at a glance” nature of this app isn’t quite there yet. 

The comments seem to indicate that more integration with multiple devices is forthcoming. Lack of this functionality is normally a dealbreaker for me, but I’m using this on my phone only for the moment because the app is just that good. At whatever point these become more integrated in the ecosystem, this and WaterMinder will unquestionably be 5 star software.

title: Amazing but needs some work

But it shouldn’t allow you skip more than 4 days because you set to go to the gym 3x. 

2. On habits that you set x number of times per week, I wish the habit would grey out after you’ve hit your goal for the week. Instead it just shows up the next day making you feel like you haven’t accomplished your weekly goal!. With graying it out, it’s still there if you want to complete it but at that point it would be clear that you’re doing extra. It’s disheartening to complete your weekly goal and then the next day it shows up again and your whole day will be marked as incomplete if you didn’t finish that task even though you’ve reached your goal. 

3. The app seems to get stuck on the previous day and for some reason still lets you mark habits in the past as complete. I think the whole idea of habit forming is that you shouldn’t be able to go back to the past but keep moving forward. Also it’s a bit confusing when it opens on “yesterday” 

Other than these things I love this app and hope it improves!

title: Fantastic for Chores
body:
I use HabitMinder almost as a daily to-do list, from washing and folding laundry, to keeping track of my sleep. I also use it to remind myself to update my ongoing thankfulness list, to pray, to read my Bible, to spend time with family, etc. I spent about a week using the free version on water, prayer and something else I don’t recall, before I decided to pay for it. I have like 25 habits now!

Features I love:
-It isn’t expensive; we don’t have a lot of money but we could afford this app at $7 for a lifetime.
-I can make up my own habits, such as dishes and make a phone call, set whether you want it to work with values or minutes (for laundry, I set a value of 4 steps before it is complete, for example, but for cleaning I have a timer). 
-I use it to remind me that I have to take a shower so I make time for it before I’m late to bed at night. 
-I like that I can make it colorful and choose icons when I create a habit. Most details can be customized. 
-The iPhone app compliments my apple watch really well. It allows you to see specific habits and how far complete they are if you choose, under the “complications” settings.
-keep track of stats for all habits, or for individual habits
-I added meals as an option simply because it feels good to check something off if I spent an hour or even half an hour of my time cooking or feeding my kid.

Features that could use work:
-I can’t mark timed chores as completed on the Apple Watch.
-I can’t change habits from value to time or vice versa once a habit is created.
-Doesn’t include percentages of habits partially complete in the day’s total (I would like that to be an option at least)
-No icons for some things, like laundry the only thing I could find was an icon of a jersey so folding and laundry have the same icon lol. Limited color palette. 
-the app occasionally crashes.
-no every other day option (and it messes with stats if you change it manually).

*Originally I said I can’t skip habits on the Apple Watch, but to my happiness, this turns out to be false! I received a response to this review, and they let me know that you can skip habits by selecting them on your watch, and force pressing the screen. An option to skip will appear.

Conclusion:
Honestly there is very little to criticize. My biggest problem is how overwhelming my to-do list looks when I open the app but most of it is little things. No wonder I was always falling behind. I could never keep track of all this stuff in my head! 

I also suggest this app if you are doing KonMari.

title: Habit Minder App
body:
When I’ve used my phone to remind me to do things, I either rebel or forget, and after some time I find the sounds increasingly annoying and finally get angry and turn them off.  If I’m going to forget or rebel, I might as well do it without the nagging.  

Habit minder is different.  Someone knew what they were doing when they designed it.  Instead of irritating sounds, it has cheerful tones; instead of stating what I’m supposed to do NOW, it asks questions—“Have you walked today?”  And if I have actually done the thing I’ve planned, I get to enter congratulatory “I did it!” messages.  It’s so much more pleasant and affirming!
